stories.headline: How Bueckers, Clark, Reese will impact Team USA at World Cup
stories.summary: The future is here for Team USA as Paige Bueckers, Caitlin Clark, Angel Reese and others make their debut in a major event.
stories.body:
A picture from 2017 resurfaces occasionally on social media. In it, a younger Caitlin Clark, Paige Bueckers and Aliyah Boston wear USA Basketball gear, huddling somewhere at the U.S. Olympic Training Center in Colorado Springs, Colorado, and flashing thumbs up and peace signs.

They had been in the cold tubs amid preparations for the FIBA Americas U16 Championship, Bueckers recently recalled to ESPN, probably after a dreaded two-a-day session. The photo also features Azzi Fudd -- who like the other three would later become a No. 1 WNBA draft pick -- and former Stanford standout Fran Belibi.

"We were all down bad hurting at such a young age," Bueckers said.

"I don't think any of us probably would have guessed we would have all made it [to this level], and that the WNBA is what it is now with the amount of attention that's on us," Clark told ESPN. "But at the same time, I think we would all say it's pretty cool. It's kind of like a pinch me moment."

Over the next 10 days, Clark, Bueckers and Boston will again share the court representing the United States with a slew of younger WNBA stars in Angel Reese, Kiki Iriafen and Sonia Citron at the FIBA World Cup in Berlin.

The group of transcendent players, with their on-court talent and off-court relevance, catapulted the WNBA into a new era of popularity. Now they are tasked with helping Team USA secure its 12th World Cup gold medal and fifth straight.

"There's always pride when you wear USA," Boston told ESPN. "I think it's kind of a full circle moment for us to be in the big girl jerseys now."

The future -- or as Bueckers quipped in December, the "Young and Turnt" crew -- is here. And they're perhaps even younger, and being thrown into the fire, even more than anticipated.

USA Basketball announced Monday that Team USA stalwarts A'ja Wilson and Kelsey Plum will not compete in Berlin due to health reasons. Those decisions led to Iriafen and Citron getting called up to join the group.

The U.S. women's team has six players under the age of 25, tied for the most on a USA World Cup or Olympic roster since 1994. With Rhyne Howard, 26, also on the squad, seven of the 12 players have never represented the senior national team in either major international 5-on-5 tournament, tied for the second-most such players on a USA roster since 1994.

But none of that matters when a gold medal is on the line. The standard for USA Basketball, which has lost one game at the World Cup or Olympics since 1994, remains the same -- even as it has become more difficult than ever to win on the international stage, as the United States' one-point win over France at the Paris Olympics' gold medal game illustrated.

"There's no question that the world is improving at a rapid rate," U.S. coach Kara Lawson said Tuesday. "I think it's going to be the most difficult World Cup to win that we've had because of that."

THE ORIGINS OF the "Young and Turnt" generation for USA Basketball might have come from that 2017 U16 team, but the players' arrival onto one of the sport's biggest stages was far from guaranteed.

Clark, Bueckers, Boston, Howard and Citron have all won multiple gold medals with USA Basketball at the youth level, from 2017 U16 gold in Argentina to finishing atop the podium at the 2019 U19 World Cup in Thailand, among others.

But as former USA Basketball national team director Carol Callan -- who oversaw all of the women's programs from 1996 to 2021 -- used to explain to players, those U17 and U19 World Cup teams would produce, on average, only one Olympian.

The World Cup is different from the Olympics, but "I think you could tell with those three specifically, they were all about basketball," Callan said of Clark, Bueckers and Boston. "Those three started at the top and they've maintained that. That's credit to them for not only their ability, but their drive, their mentality and the people that support them."

Howard has also been a mainstay for USA Basketball, featured on the Olympic qualifying team ahead of the Paris Games before ultimately being named to the 3x3 squad. Reese and Iriafen took less obvious paths: Iriafen first linked up with USA Basketball at December's training camp; Reese tried out for various youth national teams before making her first USA Basketball roster for the 2023 AmeriCup.

Callan said she ran into Reese at the event and "she just was so happy to be on a team, and I thought that was really great."

"You have two different ways to react to not making a team," Callan said. "One way is to just get angry and be done with it. And Angel persevered and made a team, and I can't say enough about her and how she's progressed to where she is today."

The sometimes-roundabout routes -- which for someone like Bueckers included missing significant time in college due to injury and falling out of the USA circuit -- makes being part of the senior national team now even sweeter.

"We all had different paths. We worked hard, had great faith. We just maintained our love and passion for the game," Bueckers said. "We're just grateful to be able to play at the national team level. Not everybody gets there. Not everybody has the same journey."

Added Clark: "I feel like there was just so much talent around my age group, and it's been fun to watch everybody kind of come into their own and have their own college careers and now live their dream at the professional level. ... It's just really cool, and feels like yesterday, honestly."

THE CHANGING OF the guard for USA Basketball started well before Berlin. The 2022 World Cup in Sydney was the USA's first major international competition since 2002 without Sue Bird or Diana Taurasi. Bird had announced her retirement, while Taurasi was injured.

Taurasi and Brittney Griner, who missed the 2022 World Cup while detained in Russia, were the most experienced members in Paris two years ago, though controversially neither saw much if any playing time in the final.

Breanna Stewart and Wilson had become the face of the USA Basketball dynasty, combining to win the past two MVPs at each of the Olympics and World Cup. The duo also accounted for 41% of the scoring at the Paris Games.

"We don't have that vet person; we are those people now," Stewart said recently.

Already a three-time Olympic gold medalist, Stewart, who recently turned 32, has a chance to join Bird as the only players to win four World Cup gold medals. She made her World Cup debut in 2014 at age 20.

"We are the ones who have been around the block a few times," Stewart told ESPN, "and it's exciting to help lead and guide them."

While a relatively inexperienced group, the United States is considered the favorite in Berlin, its roster loaded with young talent. Of the seven newcomers making their debut in a major international 5-on-5 competition, four were No. 1 picks in the WNBA draft and recent rookies of the year: Howard (2022), Boston (2023), Clark (2024) and Bueckers (2025).

Clark, Reese and Howard are leading the WNBA in assists (8.4), rebounds (12.4), and steals (2.4) per game, respectively. Clark and Bueckers are two of six players averaging at least 20 points. Citron and Iriafen are already multitime All-Stars despite being second-year players.

Clark, Bueckers, Reese, Howard and Iriafen already got a taste of what it's like to play for the senior national team, and Lawson, in March at the World Cup Qualifying tournament. In all, eight USA players who were in Puerto Rico -- including Chelsea Gray, Kahleah Copper and Jackie Young -- will also compete in Berlin. Clark and Bueckers were two of three players (alongside Plum) to play over 100 minutes in Puerto Rico and two of the top-four scorers for Team USA. Clark's 6.4 assists per game led the entire field, propelling her to earn MVP of the event.

Lawson has lauded Clark's play for the Indiana Fever this season, while the guard has said she hopes to be an extension of Lawson on the floor.

"They're both terrific," Lawson said while calling a WNBA game last month between Bueckers and Clark for Prime Video. "They're both about winning, which I think is the most important attribute in a player, in a great player."

While Clark and Bueckers might be the backcourt of the future, the ball is still expected to be primarily in the hands of Gray, the eldest player on the team at 33 and a two-time Olympic and 2022 World Cup gold medalist. But the younger guards will be watching closely to learn from her -- "I'll probably be annoying, I'll be asking so many questions," Bueckers said recently.

Stewart will anchor the effort in the frontcourt, but Reese, Boston and Iriafen will undoubtedly have even more responsibility now with Wilson out. Lawson has praised Reese for her impact on the glass -- her 8.0 boards in 16.7 minutes per game in Puerto Rico were second most in the tournament -- but has also said she sees the Dream star's physicality and competitive fire as translating well onto the FIBA stage.

"I just enjoy how she raises the level of a practice or of a game with her presence and with her intensity," Lawson said. "She plays with an aggression and a physicality, which I think is really important in FIBA play because there's a little more aggression and physicality that's typically allowed relative to the WNBA, and you need to have players that embrace that, and I think she's definitely one of the players on the roster that embraces that."

The combination of so much newness -- even Lawson was tabbed coach about a year ago -- and so little prep time is never ideal going into a major tournament, but that is typically how USA Basketball is forced to operate. The players and staff will lean on their time together in Puerto Rico or at training camps sprinkled across the past 10 months.

But they can also lean on the qualities that got them to Berlin. Lawson said her message to the younger players is to be themselves, and keep their mindset, confidence and belief in who they are intact no matter their role or experience.

"While they are kind of rookies, in my mind they're veterans," Callan said. "They infuse a competitiveness and an appreciation for the game that I think matches most those wily old veterans. You want some young ones that have this sort of really fun outlook on it, and I think they do [at the right times]. ... I think they'll bring a really nice mix to this team."

stories.headline: Fenerbahce: Mason Greenwood, Matteo Guendouzi subject of UEFA investigation
stories.summary: Mason Greenwood and Matteo Guendouzi are the subject of a disciplinary investigation by UEFA, Fenerbahce have confirmed.
stories.body:
Mason Greenwood and Matteo Guendouzi are the subject of a disciplinary investigation by UEFA, Fenerbahce have confirmed.

Fenerbahce's 2-1 win away at Lyon in a Champions League qualifier ended amid ugly scenes involving Greenwood and Guendouzi who both previously played for Marseille, the rivals of Lyon.

Guendouzi raised his middle finger to Lyon fans during the warmup and after the game and shouted "Allez l'OM" ("Go Marseille"), also grabbing his crotch, in wild post-match scenes. He said Lyon fans insulted his family before and during the game.

A post-match scuffle included someone wearing Lyon club colours confronting Guendouzi, before several players became involved in an incident in the tunnel.

It was unclear if UEFA's disciplinary judges will sanction the players before Fenerbahce opens the Champions League main phase next Thursday, hosting Roma. Fenerbahce's second game is at Aston Villa on Oct. 14.

A Fenerbahce statement read: "Following the UEFA Champions League playoff round second leg match, UEFA has initiated disciplinary proceedings against our players Matteo Guendouzi and Mason Greenwood, as well as against our club.

"Our club will present the necessary defences before the relevant UEFA bodies in order to protect the rights and interests of our players and Fenerbahce during this process.

"The necessary information, documents and defences regarding the process will be submitted to UEFA, and developments are being closely monitored by our club. We hereby inform the public."

Fenerbahce qualified for the Champions League for the first time since 2008-09 at Lyon's expense after a 3-2 aggregate win.

Former Manchester United striker Greenwood joined the Turkish club this summer from Marseille in a €39 million ($44.5m) deal.

- Aston Villa's Champions League draw: Paris Saint-Germain, Barcelona, Borussia Dortmund

- Man United's Champions League draw: Bayern Munich, Atlético Madrid, Roma

Associated Press contributed to this report.

stories.headline: Song Yadong rises in divisional rankings after shocking KO
stories.summary: Here's a look at every weight class to determine the best of the best in UFC, PFL and beyond.
stories.body:
Song Yadong scored the biggest victory of his career on Saturday at UFC Fight Night in Shanghai, knocking out onetime men's bantamweight title challenger Umar Nurmagomedov. The stunning second-round finish as a nearly 5-1 underdog propelled Song up three spots into the top four in the ESPN divisional rankings.

Nurmagomedov, who previously owned the No. 4 position at 135-pounds, slips down one spot, as do the other two fighters who had been ranked ahead of Song, Mario Bautista and Cory Sandhagen.

That was this week's only movement in the divisional rankings.

Here are the ESPN pound-for-pound MMA rankings and a list of current UFC champions in all weight classes.

stories.headline: Broncos fall to 45-year low despite defeating Bulldogs
stories.summary: Canterbury have rolled over with a whimper in their final NRL regular-season game as the Bulldogs fell to Brisbane in a 34-20 defeat.
stories.body:
Brisbane have brought the curtain down on their miserable NRL premiership defence with a 34-20 victory over Canterbury.

Eleven months on from their drought-breaking title, the Broncos returned to Accor Stadium on Thursday and sent Payne Haas out as a winner in his final Brisbane game before he joins South Sydney.

Haas, one of the heroes of last year's premiership, scored the opening try and was sent to the sin bin in an eventful first half that ended 10-10.

But after halftime Brisbane, who have been out of finals contention for weeks, pulled away and piled on 24 second-half points.

The victory was just Brisbane's eighth for the season, in what represents the worst return of any defending premiers since Canterbury in 1981.

The Broncos are just the third side in the NRL era to miss the finals in the year after a premiership.

Winger Josiah Karapani was a standout for the Broncos on Thursday, scoring two tries, chalking up 142m and 13 tackle busts as Canterbury's season ended with a whimper.

A large contingent of Bulldogs fans in the official crowd of 13,802 headed for the exit on the hour mark, and it would be hard to blame them after a year when it felt Canterbury took a step backwards by missing out on the top eight.

As has been the case for much of this season, the Bulldogs' attack was pedestrian and laboured, and even with 38 play-the-balls in Brisbane's 20m zone they struggled to threaten in possession.

Halfback Lachlan Galvin was one of those try-scorers - hitting back after Haas and Karapani gave Brisbane an early lead - but his suitability to wear the No. 7 alongside Stephen Crichton at five-eighth is sure to be a dominant storyline over the off-season.

Crichton had a hand in Canterbury's second through left winger Enari Tuala to level the scores going into halftime, but Brisbane kicked on from there.

Billy Walters, Ben Hunt, Jordan Riki and Karapani all touched down in the 20 minutes after halftime to give Brisbane their third win since a round-eight defeat of the Bulldogs in April.

Viliame Kikau and Galvin scored two late tries to reduce the deficit, but the fulltime scoreline flattered Canterbury, who finish the year with an 11-13 record.

stories.headline: Fernando Alonso uncertain on future: 'This is not the Formula 1 we grew up with'
stories.summary: Fernando Alonso has said his decision on whether to keep racing into 2027 with Aston Martin is still not made because "this is not the Formula 1 we grew up with."
stories.body:
Fernando Alonso has said his decision on whether to keep racing into 2027 with Aston Martin is still not made because "this is not the Formula 1 we grew up with."

Alonso's contract expires at the end of the current season and the 45-year-old has not committed to staying on.

Alonso has been one of the most out-spoken drivers about F1's new engine regulations -- which he has called the "battery world championship" because of the shift towards the electrical elements in the new hybrid engines.

Making matters worse for him was that Aston Martin has started the new rules cycle in horrible shape, with engine partner Honda massively off the pace, although Alonso managed to finish ninth at the Dutch Grand Prix, where the Japanese manufacturer introduced its first major upgrade of the season.

Alonso suggested there is a lot more stopping him from committing to a 25th season on the grid.

"For my decision it is not really about the [Aston Martin] car," Alonso said when probed on his future. "I will be professional and working at my 100%, fighting for P15 or fighting for a podium. But for me it is more about the regulations.

"Unfortunately, this is what it is. This is not the Formula 1 we grew up with. This is not the Formula 1 that we all want, drivers, spectators. So we must change a few things, it will not happen immediately. It will happen for the future. But I hope I can contribute somehow for the next set of regulations and we can go back to the real Formula 1."

Monza's Italian Grand Prix looks set to be another brutal run-out for F1's much-maligned new cars, with the layout of the circuit likely to expose the limitations of the battery elements of the new engine.

Asked if it would be up there with Suzuka and Silverstone, Alonso said: "Worse."

On whether it would be the worst of the year, he shrugged and said: "Maybe [not as bad as] Vegas."

- Monza personifies the passion that enticed Leclerc to commit his future to Ferrari

- Lightning McQueen to make F1 debut at Italian GP as safety car also gets Cars makeover

- Why does the Italian GP trophy look like a pile of washing up?

Alonso is the biggest name remaining on the driver market currently, but his options appear to be to stay with Aston Martin or retire -- Alpine's extension for Franco Colapinto, confirmed last week, closed off his most likely route out of Aston Martin should he want to take it.

Aston Martin has still promised to introduce at least one more car upgrade, while Honda's new package will be properly tested this weekend in Monza.

Although happy to have returned his colleagues to the points-paying positions, Alonso said a lot more needs to come before the end of the season to convince him to have another season of racing.

"No," he said when asked if P9 was enough for him to consider continuing. "We cannot be happy just with P9 and I think no one is happy in the team.

"It was a nice boost for everyone knowing that at least the direction that we are taking is the right one. Because we changed a lot of things in the car since Budapest. And obviously we know, we feel that in the corners we are getting in a much better place.

"So that gives hope for everyone in Silverstone that if we keep on going on this philosophy and this strategy and this pace of development, eventually we will be one of the fastest in the corners. So we tick one of the boxes. Then on the engine side, I think Zandvoort was not a big improvement to be honest.

"The drivability was a problem and the extra power was difficult to feel in Zandvoort. Maybe Monza is going to be a more true test for the engine. But it is still a long way to go."

stories.headline: Premier League sets new record for transfer spending
stories.summary: The Premier League set a new record for transfer spending as the window closed with a flurry of deals.
stories.body:
The Premier League set a new record for transfer spending as the window closed with a flurry of deals.

More than half of the top flight's clubs broke their transfer records in a summer window featuring four of the most expensive ever signings.

The final two days of the window pushed summer spending significantly beyond last season's record of £3.14 billion ($4.23bn) with confirmed figures exceeding £3.3b ($4.4bn).

First Liverpool spent an initial £106 million ($144m) potentially rising to £123m ($165m) on Paris Saint-Germain winger Bradley Barcola, then City paired Elliot Anderson with another nine-figure midfielder in former Chelsea star Enzo Fernández -- whose £125m ($168m) move matched the British record set 12 months ago by Barcola's new teammate Alexander Isak.

Earlier in the summer, England internationals Anderson and Morgan Rogers joined Manchester City for £116m ($156m) and Chelsea for £117m ($157m) respectively.

Sandro Tonali's move from Newcastle to Tottenham has the potential to become a fifth £100m-plus ($134.8m-plus) deal this summer, with the initial £92.5m ($124.6m) marking the second time Spurs had broken their club record as it came hot on the heels of Mateus Fernandes' £85m ($114.5m) arrival from West Ham.

Savio's £75m ($101m) switch from City slotted in third on Spurs' all-time list, with manager Roberto De Zerbi admitting "the transfer market is crazy" -- reflecting a league-wide summer of spending.

Eleven clubs in all have broken their transfer records, six of them on more than one occasion.

Coventry have done so four times over, signing Aurèle Amenda for an initial £15.4m ($20.7m) before Loum Tchaouna became their first ever £20m ($26m) signing, Carl Rushworth made his loan move permanent for a £22.5m ($30.3m) fee and Caleb Yirenkyi nudged the record up to £23.1m ($31m.)

Three clubs broke their transfer records to sign goalkeepers, with James Trafford costing Leeds £40m ($53.9m) while, like Rushworth, Konstantinos Tsolakis' move to Hull was overtaken by Nobel Mendy's £22m ($29.6m) arrival.

Aston Villa and Ipswich are the other clubs to break their respective records twice while Mamadou Sangare (Brentford), Luka Vuskovic (Brighton) and Liam Delap (Nottingham Forest) were all £40m-plus ($53.9m-plus) club-record buys.

- Man City sign Enzo Fernández from Chelsea for joint-record fee

- Premier League transfers: Under-the-radar deals you missed - but need to know about

- Chelsea, Real Madrid win transfer window; Liverpool biggest losers

There have been nine moves worth an initial £75m ($101m) or more -- a list completed by City and Arsenal midfielders Ayyoub Bouaddi and Bruno Guimarães -- plus £65m ($87m) moves for Carlos Baleba to Manchester United and Nicolas Jackson to Aston Villa.

On the other side of the balance sheet, Newcastle raised over £235m ($316m) from the three sales of Tonali, Guimaraes and Anthony Gordon while Villa banked £50m-plus ($67m-plus) fees for Ezri Konsa and Ollie Watkins in addition to Rogers' Chelsea.

It was also a record-breaking transfer window worldwide, seeing an increase in the amount of money spent and a greater number of moves than last year.

Fees topped than more £7.24bn ($9.8bn), up more than 1.5% on 12 months ago, with the number of transfers rising by 6% to 12,575, setting a new mark for the mid-year window.

According to figures released in FIFA's International Transfer Snapshot, English clubs led global spending, with more than £2.2bn ($3bn) invested in transfer fees, ahead of Italy (£810million), Spain (£695m), Germany (£668m) and France (£474m).

stories.headline: Fantasy hockey drafts: Which player should you take with the first pick?
stories.summary: Picking first? Here are the players you should consider with the No. 1 overall pick in fantasy hockey drafts.
stories.body:
Before mining the draft for valuable sleepers, potential overachievers and breakout candidates, first you have to grab the Shohei Ohtani, Jahmyr Gibbs, Taylor Swift, if you will, of the fantasy hockey world. The megastar to drive your team bus by reliably piling up more points on the daily than anyone else.

I can't remember another season where whittling down the list of eligible candidates to go first overall was so clear-cut. While I forced myself to make positive arguments for several other players as a necessary exercise, each member of the following quartet always emerged superior. So, in loose order, here's who to draft if you're fortunate to do so early on.

Please note that each player's strength is assessed within the framework of ESPN's standard H2H points game, in step with the following formula:

Skaters:

Goals = 2 points

Assists = 1 point

Shots and Hits = 0.1 points

Blocked shots and Special-teams points = 0.5 points

More: Sign up today | Rankings | Projections | Which league is right for you?

Nathan MacKinnon, F, Colorado Avalanche
I'll keep this short because his numbers are superlatively sweet. The Colorado center checks all relevant fantasy boxes, most with extra aplomb. Firing on net more often than anyone else for the third straight year, MacKinnon racked up 74 assists and 30 power-play points on 350 shots, while earning a sufficient number of hits and blocked shots to satisfy any demanding fantasy player. In this space last year, I suggested managers draft MacKinnon first overall and "hope he scores closer to 51 [goals] like in 2023-24." Well, he rifled home 53. Only Connor McDavid equaled MacKinnon in averaging 3.2 fantasy points per game in ESPN's standard fantasy league.

So, once more with feeling: Draft him first overall and hope he scores near 53 like last year. A total of 45 or so would also feel digestible enough.

Nikita Kucherov, F, Tampa Bay Lightning

Bit more to say here. A few weeks after securing his arguably overdue second Hart Trophy, the league's ultimate playmaker is once more ready to set the fantasy hockey world alight. No regular skater averaged more points per game (1.71) than Kucherov in 2025-26, not even that fella in Edmonton who flirted with the 140 total points mark. Exceptional terrain the elite winger might've reached himself had he not missed six games.

Never mind Kucherov doesn't fire on net as much as MacKinnon or Connor McDavid or bolster other nonscoring fantasy categories in any significant way. It's all about the production with this guy, and not just assists. In addition to providing 86 helpers this past run, he also has 44 goals to show for 76 contests. All the while delivering his fortunate managers with an average of 3.1 fantasy points/game, sharing rarefied air with only MacKinnon and McDavid in the 3.0-plus club. No reason to believe we're not in for similar numbers in 2026-27.

Plus, the 33-year-old is reliable enough nowadays. Since missing the entire 2020-21 regular season -- before, ahem, winning his second Stanley Cup a few weeks later -- then half a campaign to follow, Kucherov is serving as remarkably durable. There isn't a fantasy manager on the planet who's going to gripe about any player missing only 11 total games through four seasons. Especially when they're banging out 1.68 points/game three calendars running. Oh, and guess who's entering a contract year with the salary cap skyrocketing? Right. Even the fiercest competitors on the planet aren't immune to such extra incentivization. After MacKinnon, the Lightning star is my top fantasy pick.

Justification for selecting Kucherov first overall: His prospective power-play production. Last year's "measly" haul of 37 points with the extra skater falls well short of totals from previous seasons. Then there's the rather significant gap in quality between Tampa Bay's top unit and its second. Projecting that the elite winger sees a lot of time with the man-advantage and positively regresses back to his personal mean -- 50 power-play points through three previous campaigns -- could rationalize picking him first overall.

Macklin Celebrini, F, San Jose Sharks

It's all about the ceiling with this young man. After erupting for 45 goals and 70 assists in his second NHL season and more than holding his own at the Olympics as a teenager, Celebrini is just getting going. Growing up together with teammates Will Smith (21), Michael Misa (19) and Igor Chernyshov (20), the Ted Lindsay Award finalist is expected to take another step forward as a bigger and stronger player, equally if not bettering, his outstanding sophomore numbers. For starters, don't be surprised if he shoots more often on net, eclipsing the 300-shot mark for the first time. Proud of his 200-foot game, Celebrini could also conceivably improve on last year's total of 53 blocked shots. Those half-points add up fast.

The one fantasy concern lies in the goal-scoring department. Owning a 15.7% shooting percentage and, according to Evolving Hockey, an expected goals rate of 35 ixG, the Sharks center found the back of the net 45 times. Bit of a chasm there. Either Celebrini is just that much better, and therefore more accurate (completely plausible), or some good fortune was in play. My point is that this is why some models project Celebrini to bank approximately 40 goals -- and not 50 -- in 2026-27. Still, the lad's potential is too ripe to disregard. I'm grabbing him without hesitation, once McKinnon and Kucherov are off the board.

Justification for selecting Celebrini first overall: The Ivar Stenberg factor. Coach Ryan Warsovsky now has another option to toss alongside Celebrini at even strength and on the power play. Maybe the 2026 second overall draft pick serves as a delightful fit that brings even more out of the burgeoning superstar. If not, Warsofsky has many other talented and maturing options, even with William Eklund gone for Ottawa.

Connor McDavid, F, Edmonton Oilers

I know what you're thinking: What fantasy manager in their right mind would bypass the best player in our known universe with the second or, my goodness, third draft pick in any conventional league. I get the bewilderment, but hear me out. First of all, this teeny slide is less a knock on McDavid himself and more a reflection of the three preceding names and their dynamite potential in 2026-27.

Then there's the Oilers' power play to think about. Leading the league with a success rate of 30.6%, Edmonton's special teams unit will be hard-pressed to replicate that outstanding figure. Which means McDavid can't again count on nearing a tally of 54 points with the extra skater. Of course he makes Edmonton's unit better. Still, another 54-plus is a big ask for a player who has averaged about half a power-play point per game in his career, including the ridiculous Mario Lemieux-esque haul of 71 in 2021-22.

Another fantasy concern is the influence of the new guy behind the bench. Recognized for his commitment to greater defensive accountability and balancing lines and ice time, Mike Babcock isn't a fan of wild, open offensive play. Of course, he's still going to let McDavid cook, but more likely with the gas turned up to eight instead of 10. This is the coach both the megastar center and Leon Draisaitl wanted. While they won't give a lick about reduced personal numbers if it leads to a Cup, fantasy managers should still slightly temper their expectations.

Justification for selecting McDavid first overall: Because he's Connor McDavid, that's why. In the face of each logic-driven and exceptionally rational argument above, he could still magically score 140 points in 84 healthy games.

stories.headline: 2026 FIBA Women's World Cup: Team USA analysis, rankings, rosters
stories.summary: Sixteen nations will compete in the World Cup in Berlin starting Friday. Team USA and France are front-runners.
stories.body:
The WNBA season is paused for the next couple of weeks, but there's plenty of women's basketball being played. The 2026 FIBA World Cup begins Friday and will run through Sept. 13 in Berlin, Germany. The tournament might not be as prominent as the Olympics -- to fans, at least -- but it is one of two major international competitions, with this year's event featuring 16 teams from North America, Europe, Asia and Africa.

The United States is, per usual, stacked, though the reigning champions suffered a blow when it was announced Monday that four-time WNBA MVP A'ja Wilson and five-time All-Star Kelsey Plum are unable to participate in the tournament due to health reasons. But those losses don't alter the task at hand: bringing home a fifth consecutive World Cup gold and 12th overall.

The U.S. women's national team plays its group phase opener Friday against China. The USA faces Italy on Sunday and then Czechia on Monday. If the U.S. women win their group, they move on to the quarterfinals on Sept. 10, with the semifinals set for Sept. 12 and the championship and third-place games on Sept. 13.

There are plenty of other familiar faces in Berlin, too, with dozens of current and former WNBA players representing other countries, from Australia to Türkiye.

ESPN's World Cup guide gets you set with everything you need to know before the games tip. Not every roster has been finalized yet, but we list current WNBA players on each squad, along with their stats for this current WNBA season.

Jump to:

HUN | ITA | JPN | KOR | MLI | NGR

PUR | ESP | TUR | USA | GROUPS

1. United States
Current WNBA players:

F/C Aliyah Boston, Indiana Fever (16.9 PPG, 8.3 RPG, 1.3 BPG)

F Breanna Stewart, New York Liberty (20.4 PPG, 8.1 RPG, 1.4 BPG)

G Jackie Young, Las Vegas Aces (18.9 PPG, 6.6 APG, 4.4 RPG)

Outlook: The U.S. women's national basketball team is home to one of the most dominant dynasties in all of sports, winning eight consecutive Olympic gold medals and four straight World Cups. The program has lost just one game at a major international competition since 1994 -- the semifinals of the 2006 World Championship (later renamed World Cup) against Russia, where the Americans won bronze. Team USA has since won 30 consecutive World Cup games.

That is the legacy newly minted national team director Sue Bird, senior national team coach Kara Lawson and this young U.S. squad -- a group with seven players under 27 -- bring to Berlin. Fans have long anticipated seeing the likes of Clark, Bueckers and Reese compete against international competition as part of the senior national team. They got a taste of that at the World Cup qualifying tournament, where the USA went 5-0 and won by an average margin of 42 points.

But between the grueling schedule, heighted competition and pressure of representing the USA, the World Cup will be a much greater challenge. USA Basketball's youth movement will be tested even more so with Wilson, the reigning World Cup and Olympics MVP, and Plum no longer available. But they still have a core of experienced veterans in Stewart, Gray, Collier, Young and Copper, who know what it takes to win gold. -- Alexa Philippou

2. France
Current WNBA players:

G Pauline Astier, New York Liberty (9.2 PPG, 2.5 RPG, 3.4 APG)

F Valeriane Ayayi, Phoenix Mercury (6.3 PPG, 2.7 RPG, 1.3 APG)

G Marine Johannes, New York Liberty (8.5 PPG, 2.1 RPG, 2.4 APG)

G Leila Lacan, Connecticut Sun (11.6 PPG, 1.9 RPG, 4.6 APG)

G Carla Leite, Portland Fire (15.9 PPG, 2.1 RPG, 6.3 APG)

C Dominique Malonga, Seattle Storm (17.0 PPG, 9.0 RPG, 1.5 BPG)

F Janelle Salaun, Golden State Valkyries (12.9 PPG, 3.9 RPG, 1.2 APG)

G Gabby Williams, Golden State Valkyries (14.3 PPG, 3.3 RPG, 2.2 APG)

Other notable players: C Marieme Badiane

Outlook: France, seen as the top threat to Team USA, might have its most talented roster ever with eight active WNBA players, four of whom will be headed to the playoffs. France has been building as an international power for the last several years. The French nearly toppled Team USA in the Olympic final in Paris in 2024, falling 67-66 behind former UConn star Williams' 19 points. France also took Olympic silver in 2012 and bronze in 2021.

France's only medal in the World Cup was a bronze in 1953, the first year of the event, but they are expected to have a podium finish this year. Malonga, the 2025 No. 2 WNBA draft pick who dunked in the All-Star Game in July, might look to do that in the World Cup. -- Michael Voepel

3. Spain

Current WNBA players:

G Elena Buenavida, Minnesota Lynx (developmental player)

C Raquel Carrera, New York Liberty (1.4 PPG, 1.1 RPG, 0.3 APG)

F Maria Conde, Toronto Tempo (8.9 PPG, 4.6 RPG, 2.6 APG)

C Megan DiLeo, Portland Fire (13.2 PPG, 4.2 RPG, 0.6 BPG)

C Awa Fam, Seattle Storm (10.3 PPG, 5.7 RPG, 0.9 SPG)

G Alicia Florez, Washington Mystics (3.3 PPG, 2.0 APG, 0.6 SPG)

Other notable players: G Iyana Martin, G Maite Cazorla

Outlook: Spain has had a relatively quiet output on the international stage in recent years. They medaled at the World Cup in 2010, 2014 and 2018 and took silver at the 2016 Olympics -- but then didn't even qualify for the previous World Cup in 2022 or the podium in Paris.

Coming off a silver-medal finish at last year's EuroBasket -- and more recently giving the USA its closest game of March's qualifying tournament -- Spain could be poised for a big showing in Berlin. The team is led by veteran Alba Torrens, the only player with World Cup experience, and has a naturalized star in DiLeo, who was a top-five scorer at the 2024 Olympics. Carrera has seen limited time with the Liberty but has been much more productive with her national team. What might be most anticipated, though, is the emergence of Spain's young tandem of 20-year-old stars in Storm rookie Fam and Martin, the Fire's draft-and-stash first-round selection. -- Philippou

4. Belgium

Current WNBA players:

G Julie Allemand, Toronto Tempo (6.3 PPG, 3.1 RPG, 5.6 APG)

C Kyara Linskens, Phoenix Mercury (3.0 PPG, 2.4 RPG, 0.7 BPG)

F Antonia Delaere, Minnesota Lynx (2.9 PPG, 0.7 RPG, 1.1 APG)

Other notable players: F Emma Meesseman, G Julie Vanloo, F Bethy Mununga

Outlook: Belgium should be one of the powers of Group C, along with Australia. The Cats are coached by longtime former WNBA coach Mike Thibault, who won a title with the Washington Mystics in 2019 when Meesseman was WNBA Finals MVP. Meesseman has played nine seasons in the WNBA, most recently last year when she spent 20 games (including the playoffs) with the New York Liberty. Vanloo played briefly (five games) with the Liberty this season. This is Allemand's fourth season in the WNBA, and she has been a starter for the expansion Tempo. This is Belgium's third World Cup appearance; they finished fourth in 2018 and fifth in 2022. Belgium has not medaled at the Olympics but had its best finish in Paris in 2024, falling in the bronze medal game. -- Voepel

5. Germany

Projected WNBA players:

F Frieda Buhner, Portland Fire (6.3 PPG, 2.2 RPG, 0.7 APG)

G Leonie Fiebich, New York Liberty (10.2 PPG, 3.0 RPG, 1.1 SPG)

C Luisa Geiselsoder, Portland Fire (4.5 PPG, 2.6 RPG, 1.3 APG)

F Nyara Sabally, Toronto Tempo (12.3 PPG, 5.3 RPG, 0.9 BPG)

* Roster not yet finalized

Outlook: Just like in the Olympics, a World Cup host faces a mixture of pressure and opportunity, and it's no different for Germany in what is just its second time participating in the event (and first since 1998). Unfortunately the Germans will be without the services of star Satou Sabally, who has stepped away from basketball while recovering from the effects of her second concussion in eight months, and it's unclear how healthy her sister, Nyara, will be. For the Germans to earn their first podium finish at a major international competition, they will need a huge tournament from Fiebich, who has been showcasing her value with the Liberty upon returning from injury. But also expect the likes of Buhner and Geiselsoder to play even bigger roles than they do stateside in Portland. Germany is coached by Olaf Lange, current Tempo associate head coach and Sandy Brondello's husband. -- Philippou

6. China

Projected WNBA players:

C Han Xu, New York Liberty (6.4 PPG, 2.6 RPG, 0.7 BPG)

* Roster is not yet finalized

Outlook: China should be the toughest challenger to Team USA in Group D, and the two play in the event opener for both. But the team was dealt a blow Wednesday when 6-foot-7 Dallas Wings center Li Yueru said on social media she will not be competing in Berlin because her passport was lost in the mail.

The United States and China faced off twice at the 2022 World Cup, with the U.S. women winning by 14 in group play and by 22 in the gold medal match. That result was still a win for the Chinese, though, as it marked the first time since 1994 that they earned a medal at a major international competition (both were silvers).

China faltered at the 2024 Olympics, finishing in ninth, before punching its ticket to the World Cup at this spring's qualifying tournament in Wuhan. This roster has some new faces compared to that '22 squad, headlined by the 7-foot-2, 19-year-old Zhang Ziyu. But she's not the only player who could pose some trouble for the USA, as the more experienced Han Xu (6-11) brings additional height. -- Philippou

7. Australia

Current WNBA players:

F Chloe Bibby, Minnesota Lynx (2.3 PPG, 0.7 RPG, 0.7 BPG)

G Isobel Borlase, Atlanta Dream (4.6 PPG, 1.5 RPG, 1.0 APG)

C Ezi Magbegor, Seattle Storm (6.9 PPG, 4.0 RPG, 1.2 BPG)

G Jade Melbourne, Seattle Storm (9.5 PPG, 2.2 RPG, 3.9 APG)

F Alanna Smith, Dallas Wings (6.0 PPG, 3.9 RPG, 1.0 APG)

G Miela Sowah, Golden State Valkyries (0.3 PPG, 0.8 RPG)

F Stephanie Talbot, Las Vegas Aces (3.5 PPG, 2.6 RPG, 1.0 APG)

Other notable players: F Alex Fowler, G Alex Wilson

Outlook: Phoenix Mercury guard Sami Whitcomb, captain of the Australian team, had to withdraw from the World Cup last week because of an ongoing knee injury. It's a big blow to the Opals regarding leadership and scoring. And it's heartbreaking for Whitcomb, who is 38. She was replaced by Sowah, 26. Sandy Brondello, who won WNBA titles with the Mercury (2014) and New York Liberty (2024) and is now with the Toronto Tempo, is Australia's coach.

The Opals began to emerge as an international power in women's basketball in the 1980s and won their first World Cup medal with a bronze in 1998. Their highlight was 2006, when they defeated Russia for the gold medal after the Russians had upset the United States in the semifinals. They also won bronze in 2002, 2014 and 2022, and took silver in 2018. Australia's six total World Cup medals puts them third on the all-time medal chart. The Aussies also have six Olympic medals: three silvers and three bronzes. -- Voepel

8. Italy

Current WNBA players:

G Costanza Verona, Dallas Wings (developmental player)

F Cecilia Zandalasini, Golden State Valkyries (8.8 PPG, 2.2 RPG, 1.8 APG)

Other notable players: F Lorela Cubaj

Outlook: Italy is enjoying a resurgence on the FIBA stage: Last year the team won its first EuroBasket medal since 1995 by beating France for the bronze medal, and now this World Cup marks the country's first appearance at a major international competition since the 1996 Olympics. Led by Zandalasini, the Italians lost 93-59 to the United States at the qualifying tournament in Puerto Rico, but went 4-1 overall at the event, including upsetting Spain the day after playing the U.S. women (and it's largely the same squad Italy has in Berlin). Italy has a difficult path ahead, though, having to face both the USA and China, the 2022 World Cup silver medalist, in the group phase. -- Philippou

9. Nigeria

Projected WNBA players:

F Amy Okonkwo, Portland Fire (4.3 PPG, 1.0 RPG, 0.3 APG)

* Roster not yet finalized

Outlook: This is the fourth time Nigeria has qualified for the World Cup, although it withdrew in 2022. That was much to the chagrin of the Nigerian players and FIBA. It was a decision by the Nigerian government, which opted in May 2022 to withdraw all its basketball teams from international competition while it restructured the sport's governance. Nigeria earned its World Cup berth this time by winning the AfroBasket 2025 championship. The team still played in the World Cup qualifying tournament in France in March, but lost three of five games. Nigeria's best finish in the World Cup is eighth, in 2018. The team's best Olympic finish is also eighth, in 2024. -- Voepel

10. Japan

Current WNBA players:

G Mai Yamamoto, Las Vegas Aces (5.8 PPG, 1.8 APG, 0.8 SPG)

Other notable players: G Rui Machida, G Kokoro Tanaka, C Ramu Tokashiki

Outlook: American basketball fans have come to enjoy Japan's entertaining style of play in recent years, particularly since squaring off against the USA in the 2020 Olympic gold medal game. Japan is known for speed, movement and 3-point shooting, which means the team can beat anyone if it gets hot -- and can lose to anyone if it can't hit shots. Lack of size is often an Achilles' heel -- just one player, Tokashiki, is listed over 6-foot.

Still, look out for the likes of Yamamoto, a midseason addition to the Aces, as well as Golden State draft pick Tanaka to make a splash on the perimeter. After the high of clinching silver at the Tokyo Olympics, Japan finished ninth at the 2022 World Cup, 12th at the Paris Olympics and almost didn't qualify for Berlin. Corey Gaines, the coach of the 2009 Phoenix Mercury championship squad, took over as head coach in early 2025. The pressure is on for them to find their form going into 2030, when they will host the next World Cup. -- Philippou

11. Hungary

Projected WNBA players:

F Dorka Juhász, Minnesota Lynx (3.8 PPG, 2.6 RPG, 1.2 APG)

* Roster not yet finalized

Outlook: While France is a big favorite in Group B, Hungary might make some waves behind Juhász. That especially could be the case with JiSu Park out for Korea and Nigeria looking kind of inconsistent entering the tournament. Hungary is making its sixth appearance in the World Cup but first since 1998. The team's best finish was fifth in 1957. -- Voepel

12. Korea

Current WNBA players:

G Jihyun Park, Los Angeles Sparks (2.2 PPG, 1.0 RPG, 0.5 APG)

Outlook: Korea is typically known as a strong outside shooting team. The team will need to rely even more on its guards with center JiSu Park, who played three seasons with the Las Vegas Aces, out due to an ankle injury. Korea is making its 18th World Cup appearance; it has played in every tournament except the first two in 1953 and 1957. Korea has won two silver medals, in 1967 and 1979. The team also has finished fourth three times, most recently in 2002. Korea has one medal in Olympic play, a silver in 1984. -- Voepel

13. Türkiye

Projected WNBA players:

G/F Kennedy Burke, Connecticut Sun (8.8 PPG, 3.2 RPG, 1.4 APG)

* Roster not yet finalized

Outlook: Türkiye will learn a lot about its chances from its opener vs. Belgium. This is Türkiye's third appearance in the World Cup; the team was fourth in 2014, when it hosted the event, and 10th in 2018. In her seventh year in the WNBA, Burke is having a career-best season. -- Voepel

14. Mali

Projected WNBA players:

G Aicha Coulibaly, Chicago Sky (4.8 PPG, 2.8 RPG, 0.7 SPG)

F Sika Kone, Atlanta Dream (1.7 PPG, 1.0 RPG)

* Roster not yet finalized

Outlook: Mali will make its third World Cup appearance, where it hopes to improve on an 11th-place finish in 2022. The program established itself as the second-best team out of Africa behind Nigeria, which beat Mali in the 2025 AfroBasket final. But Mali followed that up with a promising showing during the qualifying tournament in March, beating Czechia and narrowly losing to Brazil to clinch a spot in Berlin. Maimouna Haidara was the team's leading scorer in Wuhan, followed by the Dream's Kone; they'll need those two to dazzle to cause some upsets in Group A. -- Philippou

15. Czechia

Current WNBA players:

G Eliska Joklova, Minnesota Lynx (1.7 PPG, 1.1 APG, 1.0 RPG)

Outlook: Czechia is back at the World Cup after last appearing in the event in 2014; in 2010, it was the host nation and earned silver. The team's return this year has already been met with some concern. Czechia eked into the World Cup after a tepid qualifying tournament and has had some bad injury luck to two key players: Emma Cechova tore her ACL three games into her season with the Minnesota Lynx after a promising start, while Julia Reisingerova is also unavailable due to injury. On top of that, Czechia has to face the United States, China and a surging Italy squad in group play. It'll need sensational outings from the likes of Lynx rookie Joklova (née Hamzova), Veronika Vorackova and Petra Holesinska to keep up. -- Philippou

16. Puerto Rico

Current WNBA players: None

Other notable players: G Arella Guirantes, C Imani McGee-Stafford

Outlook: Host Puerto Rico was fourth in the qualifying tournament won by the United States in March in San Juan. A tough group awaits in Berlin, especially having to face Australia and Belgium. This is Puerto Rico's third appearance in the World Cup, having finished 16th in 2018 and eighth in 2022. Guirantes played two seasons in the WNBA, most recently in 2023. McGee-Stafford played four seasons in the league, most recently in 2019. Puerto Rico has competed twice in the Olympics. -- Voepel

Groups

Sixteen teams will compete in the FIBA World Cup in Berlin, Germany, with 36 games being played over 10 days from Sept. 4 to Sept. 13. The first-place team in each group advances to the quarterfinals; the second- and third-place teams will qualify for a single-game elimination format to determine the rest of the quarterfinalists.

stories.headline: Song Yadong KO's Umar Nurmagomedov in massive UFC upset
stories.summary: Song Yadong pulled off a massive upset by knocking out heavily favored Umar Nurmagomedov in the men's bantamweight main event of UFC Fight Night in Shanghai.
stories.body:
Song Yadong saved the greatest performance of his career for his home country, knocking out former title challenger Umar Nurmagomedov in the men's bantamweight main event of UFC Fight Night on Saturday in Shanghai.

Song (24-9-1, 1 NC), a nearly 5-1 underdog at DraftKings Sportsbook, dropped Nurmagomedov with a short right hand, drawing a roar from the crowd when the fight was waved off at 1 minute, 48 seconds of Round 2.

"I believe in myself, and my team believed that I would win this fight," Song said through an interpreter. "They told me I would knock this guy out, and I did it."

It was the second straight fight in China for Song and his second straight win by finish. His most recent knockout win had been in 2023.

Song, making his first appearance in Shanghai since his UFC debut at age 19 in 2017, walked out to a hero's welcome.

"Nine years ago, I wanted to show I could walk in this Octagon," he said. "Nine years later, I want to prove I am the best in the world. I am the best Chinese fighter in the world."

The knockout came after Nurmagomedov (20-2) ducked out of the way of a left hand and right into the path of a short right hand, which connected near his right ear and sent him limply to the canvas. Song delivered three finishing shots on the mat before the referee jumped in.

That sent Song running around inside the cage in celebration, where he nearly ran into Nurmagomedov's younger brother and cornerman, PFL lightweight champion Usman Nurmagomedov, who had rushed in to check on his fallen brother. Usman Nurmagomedov appeared to throw an elbow in Song's direction as the elated winner was running past.

Song climbed atop the cage to soak in the fans' cheers before jumping down outside the cage and running into the crowd to get hugs and high-fives from fans.

"Maybe not today, maybe not tomorrow, maybe not next month, but I will be the first male Chinese UFC champion," Song said through the interpreter, with the "male" designation a nod to countrywoman Zhang Weili, a two-time women's champion at strawweight.

Song, who trains in Sacramento, California, switched to English and yelled, "Give me the title shot!"

stories.headline: State of Origin: Darius Boyd replaces Billy Slater as Queensland coach
stories.summary: Queensland's search for a new State of Origin coach is over, with Maroons legend Darius Boyd to take over in 2027 after signing a two-year deal.
stories.body:
Former Queensland star Darius Boyd will lean on the legacy and advice of former mentors Mal Meninga and Wayne Bennett after being appointed as the new Maroons coach.

The Queensland Rugby League confirmed on Thursday that Boyd would take up the position in 2027 on a two-year deal after Billy Slater stepped down from the role after five years.

Boyd, who won NRL premierships with Brisbane and St George Illawarra in a 337-game career, played 28 State of Origin matches for the Maroons and was a key figure in the dynasty under Meninga.

As a coach Boyd has led the Queensland U19 team to wins in back-to-back interstate clashes after being a member of the coaching staff at the Broncos under Kevin Walters for three seasons.

Boyd, who also played 23 Tests for Australia, said he was "extremely honoured" to be entrusted with coaching Queensland's State of Origin team.

"It's a privileged position and I'm very grateful for the opportunity," Boyd said.

"I understand the responsibility that comes with the role as well. My job is to build on the legacy created by the many great Queensland players and coaches who have come before us."

Boyd, who said Slater had left behind a wonderful program to build on, will make a call on his staff in the future, but said those who "live and breathe" for the jersey will be at the top of his list.

He played most of his career under his lifelong mentor Wayne Bennett, who has said he would assist the new coach where he can.

"He is the supercoach. I would be silly not to get his advice on things," Boyd said when asked if Bennett would be on his team.

Meninga, who coached Boyd in the glory years, also shaped the way he will approach the task.

Boyd said that "the history and what it meant to play for Queensland and how Origin started and the legacy those guys left behind" was a key message of Meninga that got the best out of the Maroons.

"It is a challenging job to be out in the cauldron and play at the highest level and perform at your best," Boyd said.

"Mal was really good at getting the best out of you emotionally and mentally and making sure you were prepared come game night."

QRL chairman Brian Canavan said once Slater stepped down after winning three of five series, the organisation came up with a list of candidates and Boyd was the standout.

"If you go back five years ago Billy was at the same point," he said.

"He hadn't had the formal NRL coaching experience. Darius has more experience than Billy had back then. That gave us confidence to go to a new phase.

"Billy has left the place and program in great shape, and Darius will step in and put his own spin on things.":

Bennett was a great support on and off the field to Boyd and will be there to lean on.

"The advice Wayne offered was that he would support whoever we appointed, and Wayne has had a long association with Darius and knows his great strengths," Canavan said.

"The most important thing for this job is the identity with the state.

"What he has got is the pride and passion for the jersey and the state and this connection with players and appetite for the historical aspects of the jersey and embedding it in players."

Boyd entered a mental health facility at a key moment in his NRL career and has since been a leader in that space.

It was a turning point and he now understands the mental side of life and footy.

"It has been a journey for me on and off the field. It is a great opportunity for me to instil belief, confidence and desire into the next generation," he said.
